clue.text: Daughter wearing insane headgear

indicators.note: the insane word is wearing the daughter, holding her inside it like a garment

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy or insane

explanation.surface: A daughter has turned up wearing some wild, crazy hat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wearing' puts D inside BANANAS, splitting it as BAN-D-ANAS.
explanation.definitionFit: Bandanas are large patterned kerchiefs tied over the head, so they count as headgear.

clue.text: Domain of Delaware Nation

indicators.note: the answer is taken out of the run of letters in the two words that follow

explanation.surface: The territory belonging to the Delaware, a Native American nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' signals the answer sitting inside delawARE NAtion.
explanation.definitionFit: An arena is a sphere of activity, a field or domain in which someone operates.

clue.text: Make sure Spitting Image is given European broadcast

parts.note: a spitting image of someone is their double

indicators.note: broadcast means the word is heard rather than read, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: a Czech is a European, from the Czech Republic

explanation.surface: Checking that the satirical puppet show Spitting Image gets a European TV airing.
explanation.walkthrough: Spitting Image was a British TV puppet satire, which makes 'broadcast' look like TV. Here 'broadcast' says CZECH is heard as CHECK.
explanation.definitionFit: To double-check is to verify again, making certain that something is right.

clue.text: Boxing heavyweight, raised outside Lima, eaten by bear

indicators.note: the turned word goes around the outside of what follows
in a down clue, raised means the word is written from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: a ton is a heavy weight

indicators.note: the Lima letter is swallowed by the bear, sitting inside it

parts.note: taken as written
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A boxing heavyweight from Peru's capital gets mauled by a bear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raised' (read upwards in a down clue) gives NOT; the bear holding Lima makes BLEAR, which 'outside' places between NO and T.
explanation.definitionFit: The noble art (of self-defence) is an old literary name for the sport of boxing.

clue.text: Good God! British seem upset about retired clergyman getting married

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go round what follows
upset means the letters are knocked over into a new order

parts.note: anagram fodder

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: Rev, short for Reverend, is a title for a clergyman

explanation.surface: Shocked Brits look upset because a retired vicar has got married.
explanation.walkthrough: The rearranged BRITISH SEEM splits around the inserted pieces as SHI-VER-M-ETIMBERS. Rev, for Reverend, is the usual clergy abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Shiver me timbers is a mock-pirate exclamation of surprise, much like crying out to the heavens.

clue.text: Wander aimlessly around eastern part of Thar Desert

indicators.note: the first word is placed around the letters that follow

parts.note: to moon about is to drift around listlessly

indicators.note: on a map east is the right side, so this takes the final letters of the word

explanation.surface: Drifting aimlessly across the far east of the Thar Desert in India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eastern part of' keeps only the right-hand end of Thar, since east is right on a map. 'Desert' looks like part of the desert's name but is the definition, a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To maroon someone is to abandon them somewhere isolated, which is to desert them.

clue.text: Maiden bus tour oddly avoided Alabama? It's common!

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters are skipped, leaving the even ones

parts.note: AL is the postal abbreviation for Alabama

explanation.surface: A young woman's bus tour skipped Alabama, which is apparently common.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly avoided' keeps the even letters of BUS TOUR, giving UTU.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mutual is shared by both or all parties, held in common.

clue.text: Spirit of revolutionary Greek character underpinning resistance

indicators.note: in a down answer, the second piece sits below the first, supporting it

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: The spirit of a Greek rebel shoring up the resistance movement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' turns MU into UM, which goes under R.
explanation.definitionFit: Rum is a distilled alcoholic drink, and spirits are such drinks.

clue.text: Promptly abandoned in Athlone

indicators.note: abandoned suggests wild and unrestrained, so the letters run riot

explanation.surface: Something swiftly left behind in the Irish town of Athlone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abandoned' rearranges IN ATHLONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Paying on the nail means paying at once, without delay.

clue.text: Dull bishops defending European Union

indicators.note: the bishops stand on either side, guarding what goes between them

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for a bishop, so two make BB
NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, a British trade union

explanation.surface: Boring churchmen speaking up in defence of the European Union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'European Union' reads as one body, but it splits as E + NUM; the NUM is the British miners' union.
explanation.definitionFit: To benumb is to make numb or deaden, so it means to dull the senses.

clue.text: Eventually accepting heartless act is personal

indicators.note: the first phrase takes the following letters into itself

parts.note: in time means eventually, sooner or later

indicators.note: without its heart the word keeps only its outside letters

explanation.surface: Someone finally coming round to a callous deed that is very personal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the C of ACT to give AT; 'accepting' puts it inside IN TIME.
explanation.definitionFit: Intimate matters are private and close to oneself, the same as personal ones.

clue.text: Get sick on second cruise

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece set on after another follows it

parts.note: to ail is to be or fall ill

explanation.surface: Becoming seasick on the second sea cruise.
explanation.definitionFit: To sail is to travel by boat, which is what a leisurely cruise involves.

clue.text: Covers for disused sockets?

parts.note: sockets suggests electrical outlets, but here they are the hollows that hold eyes, and an unused one may be covered

explanation.surface: Safety covers for electrical sockets nobody uses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sockets' invites plugs and wiring; the sockets are eye sockets, and the covers are what a pirate wears.
explanation.definitionFit: A patch over the eye hides an empty or injured eye socket.

clue.text: Say something to curb Left's conduct

indicators.note: to curb is to restrain, so the first word holds the other in check inside it

parts.note: to comment is to say something
port is the left side of a ship; the 's stands for is, a link

explanation.surface: Speaking out to restrain left-wing behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks political, but port is the nautical word for the left side of a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Comportment is a person's bearing or behaviour, how they conduct themselves.

clue.text: Range of Bond villains briefly united with M

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the last letter goes

parts.note: SPECTRE is the criminal organisation in the James Bond stories
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A range of Bond villains, briefly allied with M, Bond's spymaster boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'briefly' cuts SPECTRE to SPECTR; M is both Bond's boss and the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A spectrum is a full range, from one extreme to the other.

clue.text: Ship from Portugal at back of queue entering waterway

parts.note: P is the international vehicle code for Portugal

indicators.note: the preceding letters go inside the waterway

parts.note: a river is a natural waterway

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

explanation.surface: A vessel from Portugal waiting at the end of a line to pass through a canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back of' takes the last letter of queue, which joins 'at' before both go inside the waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was an armed private ship licensed by a government to attack enemy vessels.

clue.text: Chap nursing old grievance

indicators.note: the man nurses or holds the other letter inside

parts.note: a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A fellow nursing a long-held complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: A moan is a complaint, a gripe or grievance voiced aloud.

clue.text: General climbs aboard a hulk in order to punish 22?

indicators.note: the general boards the ship, going inside the other letters
put in order means the letters are rearranged
in a down clue, climbing means reading from bottom to top, so backwards

parts.note: Lee was the Confederate general in the American Civil War

explanation.surface: A general boards an old hulk to discipline the sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in order' rearranges A HULK into K…HAUL; 'climbs' turns LEE into EEL, and 'aboard' puts it in. 22 is TARS, sailors.
explanation.definitionFit: Keelhauling was a brutal naval penalty, dragging an offending sailor under the ship's keel.

clue.text: Dig earth after 11

indicators.note: the earth letter comes after the sail

parts.note: the answer to 11 is SAIL, and a jib is a kind of sail
E is the abbreviation for earth, as in electrical wiring

explanation.surface: Digging soil after something numbered eleven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dig' looks like a spade at work, but it means a taunt.
explanation.definitionFit: A jibe is a mocking remark, and a dig is a pointed jab at someone.

clue.text: Adapting Othello, Jerry incorporates German flag

indicators.note: the rearranged letters take the German letter into their body
adapting a play reshapes it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone called Jerry adapts Shakespeare's Othello and slips some German into it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Adapting' rearranges OTHELLO JERRY into THE JOLLY ROER; 'incorporates' puts G in.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jolly Roger is the traditional skull-and-crossbones flag flown by pirates.

clue.text: Articles claiming drink leads to heartache

indicators.note: the articles claim or take hold of the drink, holding it inside

parts.note: an and a are both indefinite articles
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: Newspaper pieces claiming that drinking leads to heartbreak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartache' reads as sorrow, but it is literal pain in the heart.
explanation.definitionFit: Angina is chest pain caused by poor blood flow to the heart, a literal ache of the heart.

clue.text: Butchered mink, alpaca and llama, say

indicators.note: butchered means cut up, so the letters are chopped and reassembled

explanation.surface: A mink, an alpaca and a llama are slaughtered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butchered' rearranges MINK ALPACA; 'say' marks the llama as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Llamas are used in the Andes to carry loads, the classic example of a beast of burden.

clue.text: Army recruits discontented mariners

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve

indicators.note: with its contents gone, only the outside letters of the word stay

explanation.surface: New army recruits are unhappy at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discontented' looks like a mood, but it means emptied of contents, leaving R…S.
explanation.definitionFit: Tar is old slang for a sailor, so tars are mariners.

clue.text: See 19
Pipers playing before queen start to exude sweat

indicators.note: playing means the letters are moved about freely

parts.note: R is for Regina, Latin for queen

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Bagpipers performing for the queen begin to sweat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges PIPERS into PERSPI; 'start to' gives E from exude.
explanation.definitionFit: To perspire is the polite word for giving off moisture through the skin.

clue.text: Main suspect eludes arrest initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: The chief suspect slips away from being arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective, chief; it is the old poetic noun for the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a literary word for the open ocean, as in the Spanish Main.

clue.text: Being brought up somewhere else, reportedly

indicators.note: reportedly means as reported by voice, so the sound of the word counts

parts.note: away means somewhere else, absent

explanation.surface: A child being raised far away, or so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' suggests upbringing; it is an anchor being raised.
explanation.definitionFit: An anchor is aweigh when it has just been lifted clear of the seabed.

clue.text: Task force from Irish county picked up attorney

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word's sound gives the letters

parts.note: Armagh is a county in Northern Ireland
DA is District Attorney, a US prosecutor

explanation.surface: A legal task force from County Armagh picked up a lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: ARMAGH is pronounced ar-MAH, so it sounds like ARMA.
explanation.definitionFit: An armada is a fleet of warships, a naval force sent on a mission.

clue.text: Reclusive storyteller engaging model in saucy stuff

indicators.note: the built piece goes inside the sauce

parts.note: soy is a sauce, so it is literally saucy stuff

indicators.note: to engage something is to take it in, so the storyteller holds the next letter

parts.note: a liar tells stories, untrue ones
the Model T was Ford's famous car, so T stands for model

explanation.surface: A reclusive writer hires a model for some racy material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saucy' suggests racy, but saucy stuff is a sauce. The Model T was Ford's famous car, hence model for T.
explanation.definitionFit: A solitary person lives alone and avoids company, the way a recluse does.
